newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Apr 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Apr 9.

text.p: Clear establishes new horizons: After half a century of unsuccessful proposals for the 12.5ha Smales Farm on the North Shore, the first soil has been turned for Clear Communications' $50 million new headquarters building.

Nat Bank gloomy on Govt spending: The government's planned $5 billion of extra spending over the next three years is more likely to come in at $6.5 billion due to spending creep and the effect of expected slower economic growth, National Bank economists say.
Fay and Richwhite prosper on Cultus: A huge jump in exploration company Cultus share price has left its prominent shareholders, Sir Michael Fay and David Richwhite, smiling all the way to their bank.

The Warehouse result should put bugs to bed: Ongoing computer hiccups should not stop The Warehouse Group reporting solid half-year earnings this week. Glitches with the discount retailer's new computer accounts payable to system have apparently caused temporary delays in the company paying its suppliers.
Richina in for the long haul: Richina Pacific shareholders will have to wait some time before the company's investments in China deliver the hoped-for profits chairman Jim Syme said.

Phone costs bother users: No surprise then in the findings of a Telecommunications Users Association (TUANZ) survey that commercial telephone users intend to expand telecommunications usage, but are concerned they are paying too much,
